nodes.description: Corticosteroids are not routinely recommended for miliary tuberculosis; studies of routine use are few and conflicting. They are used for specific complications: adrenal insufficiency (an absolute indication), tuberculous meningitis, pericarditis, and, with weaker evidence, ARDS, IRIS and immune-complex nephritis. In ARDS a small retrospective series found better 3-month survival with steroid pulses, while a larger ICU cohort could not determine any effect on survival.

nodes.description: Isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for two months, then isoniazid and rifampicin for four months, for drug-susceptible disease; 9-12 months when meningitis is present, and longer for bone and joint disease. There is no consensus or trial evidence on optimum duration, and organ involvement (especially meningitis and pericarditis) is assessed before starting. Drug-induced liver injury is common (15-16% in two series); an asymptomatic transaminase rise is not by itself a reason to stop, but true injury requires stopping the hepatotoxic drugs. Rifampicin lowers antiretroviral levels through CYP450 induction, so HIV regimens need adjusting.
